title: One Live Prescription per Pet, Medication and Strength at Tailwise Pharmacy
content:
*Care Academy, pharmacy module: prescription records.*

A customer may hold any number of Tailwise Pharmacy prescriptions across their pets; there is no limit on how many prescriptions one customer holds. What is limited is the number of live prescriptions for one combination of pet, medication and strength.

## The rule

1. A new prescription is opened for a pet only where no other prescription of the same customer for the same pet, medication and strength is in status pending veterinarian authorization or active. The prescription records are the authority for this: the status shown on the customer's existing prescriptions decides, not the customer's account of them.
2. A second order for the same pet, medication and strength is handled on the existing prescription — as a fill, as a package size change or, once that prescription can no longer be filled, as a renewal — and is not opened as a new prescription.
3. A different strength of the same medication is a different prescription.

The comparison is made on three things together: the pet, the medication and the strength written on the prescription.

## Cases (hypothetical)

| Existing prescription for the same pet | Order asked for | Opened as a new prescription? |
|---|---|---|
| Same medication and strength, active | same medication and strength | No; handled on the existing prescription |
| Same medication and strength, pending veterinarian authorization | same medication and strength | No; handled on the existing prescription |
| Same medication, different strength, active | the other strength | Yes, if no live prescription exists for that strength |
| Same medication and strength, for another pet of the customer | same medication and strength for this pet | Yes, if this pet has no live prescription for it |

## Training questions

**A customer already has three prescriptions for one dog and asks for a fourth, different medication. Is there a cap?**
No. A customer may hold any number of prescriptions across their pets; only a second live prescription for the same pet, medication and strength is excluded.

**The existing prescription for the same pet, medication and strength is refills exhausted or expired. Does the one-live-prescription rule stand in the way of continuing?**
The rule looks only at prescriptions pending veterinarian authorization or active. A prescription that can no longer be filled is continued by a renewal, as rule 2 states.
